judge.note: the program on the site that runs your code and checks the answer

verdict.note: the result the judge gives your code, like Accepted or Wrong answer

rating.note: a number that shows your level; it changes after each contest

contest.note: about two hours, a few new problems, many people at the same time

division.note: the level of a contest: Div. 4 is the easiest, Div. 1 the hardest

submit.note: send your code to the judge

compile.note: turn your C++ text into a program that can run

sample.note: an example input with its correct output, shown in the statement

time-limit.note: the most time your program may run on one test, often 1 or 2 seconds

memory-limit.note: the most memory your program may use, often 256 MB

runtime-error.note: the program crashed while it was running

template.note: a ready start file that you copy for every problem

product.note: the result of multiplying: the product of 3 and 4 is 12

round-up.note: go to the next whole number: 7 / 2 rounded up is 4

floating-point.note: a number like 3.14 in a double; it is not always exact

exact.note: fully correct, with no small error

upsolving.ar: حلّ المسائل التي لم تحلّها بعد انتهاء المسابقة
upsolving.note: after a contest, solve the problems you could not solve

virtual.note: do an old contest with a real timer, as if it is live

stress-test.note: run your code and a slow correct code on many random inputs and compare

random.note: chosen by chance, not by a rule

uninitialised.note: a variable that never got a start value, so it holds garbage

out-of-range.note: an index below 0 or above the last position

habit.note: something you do every time, without thinking

data-type.note: what kind of value a variable holds and how big it can be, like int or long long

checklist.note: a list of things to check, one by one, in order

sorted.note: in order, from small to big

monotonic.note: only goes one way: once it becomes yes, it stays yes

overflow.note: the number is too big for the type, so it becomes garbage

algorithm.note: a clear list of steps that solves a problem

complexity.note: how the number of steps grows when the input grows

constraints.note: the limits of the input, like 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000

index.note: the position number in an array, starts from 0

array.note: many values in a row, each with an index

subarray.note: a part of the array with no gaps

subsequence.note: some elements in the same order, gaps allowed

substring.note: a part of a string with no gaps

permutation.note: the numbers 1..n, each exactly once, in some order

greedy.note: always take the best choice right now

simulation.note: do exactly the steps the statement describes

divisible.note: a is divisible by b when a % b == 0

prime.note: a number > 1 divisible only by 1 and itself

divisor.note: d is a divisor of n when n % d == 0

parity.note: is the number even or odd

recursion.note: a function that calls itself on a smaller problem

tree.note: a connected graph with n vertices and n−1 edges, no cycles

cycle.note: a path that comes back to its start

editorial.note: the official explanation of the solution

edge-case.note: a special small or extreme input, like n = 1

modulo.note: the remainder after dividing by m

frequency.note: how many times a value appears

query.note: one question you must answer, often there are many

test-case.note: one input the judge runs your code on

variable.note: a named box that holds one value, like int n

loop.note: code that repeats, like for or while

trace.note: run the code by hand and write the variables after each step

character.note: one letter, digit or sign, like 'a' or '7'; the type is char

unsigned.note: a number type that cannot be negative; 0 − 1 becomes a huge number

round-down.note: throw away the part after the point: 7 / 2 rounded down is 3

digit.note: one of 0…9; the number 4072 has four digits

arithmetic-progression.note: numbers with the same step between neighbours, like 3, 5, 7, 9

absolute-value.note: the number without its sign: abs(−5) = 5

candidate.note: a value that may be the answer; you still have to check it

possibility.note: one of the things that can happen or can be chosen

choice.note: what you decide to take at one step

counterexample.note: one small input that shows an idea is wrong

container.note: a ready C++ box that stores many values: vector, set, map…

stack.ar: مكدّس (آخر ما يدخل أوّل ما يخرج)
stack.note: you add and remove only at the top

queue.ar: طابور (أوّل ما يدخل أوّل ما يخرج)
queue.note: you add at the back and remove from the front

key.note: the thing you search by in a map, like a name in a phone book

duplicate.note: a value that appears more than once

comparator.note: a function that says which of two elements comes first

range.note: all positions from l to r

running-sum.note: the sum of everything up to now

difference-array.note: stores only where a change starts and where it ends

pointer.note: here: just an index that walks along the array

sliding-window.note: a subarray [l, r] that moves to the right step by step

merge.note: join two sorted lists into one sorted list

gcd.note: the biggest number that divides both a and b

lcm.note: the smallest number divisible by both a and b

sieve.note: a fast way to find all primes up to n by crossing out multiples

factorisation.note: writing n as a product of primes: 60 = 2·2·3·5

square-root.note: sqrt(n): the number r with r·r = n

power.note: a^b = a multiplied by itself b times

modular-inverse.note: the number that replaces division when you work modulo m

binary.note: numbers written with only the digits 0 and 1

xor.note: 1 when the two bits are different, 0 when they are equal

mask.note: a number whose bits say which items are chosen

subset.note: some of the items (maybe none, maybe all)

precedence.note: which operator the compiler does first

constructive.note: you must build and print one valid answer

invariant.note: something that stays the same after every operation

valid.note: it follows every rule of the statement

alternating.ar: متناوب (واحد من هذا ثم واحد من ذاك)
alternating.note: two kinds that take turns: small, big, small, big…

shift.note: move every element one position, the last one goes to the start

base-case.note: the smallest problem; you answer it directly, with no more calls

backtracking.note: try a choice, go deeper, then undo the choice and try the next one

call-tree.note: a drawing of which call makes which calls

dynamic-programming.note: solve small problems once, store the answers, build big answers from them

subproblem.note: a smaller copy of the same problem

state.note: the numbers that describe one subproblem, like i in dp[i]

transition.note: the formula that builds dp[i] from smaller answers

memoisation.note: store the answer of a call so you never compute it twice

knapsack.note: choose items with the best total value so the total weight fits in the bag

adjacency-list.note: for every vertex, the list of its neighbours

neighbour.note: a vertex joined to this vertex by one edge

visited.note: a mark that says: I was already here

connected.note: you can walk from any vertex to any other vertex

connected-component.note: a group of vertices that can all reach each other

dfs.note: go as deep as you can, then come back

bfs.note: visit level by level: first distance 1, then 2, then 3…

undirected.note: you can use the edge in both directions

directed.note: the edge goes one way only, from a to b

path.note: a walk from one vertex to another along edges

shortest-path.note: the path with the smallest length (or smallest total weight)

grid.note: a table of cells with rows and columns

weight.note: the number written on an edge: its length or cost

priority-queue.note: a container that always gives you the smallest (or biggest) element first

root.note: the top vertex of a tree; everything hangs from it

parent.note: the vertex directly above this one

child.note: a vertex directly below this one

depth.note: the number of edges from the root to this vertex

subtree.note: a vertex together with everything below it

diameter.note: the longest path between two vertices of the tree

leader.note: the one element that stands for its whole group

path-compression.note: after find(x), x points straight to the leader, so the next find is fast

in-degree.ar: درجة الدخول (عدد الأسهم الداخلة إلى الرأس)
in-degree.note: how many arrows point to this vertex

topological-order.note: an order of the vertices where every arrow goes from left to right

combination.note: a way to choose r items from n when order does not matter

precompute.note: calculate once at the start, then reuse many times

interactive.note: your program and the judge send messages to each other

flush.note: send the printed text now, do not keep it in memory
